newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 28.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

President Chandrika Kumaratunga said that perpetrators of violence who threaten fundamental and political liberties will be delt with sternly. She spoke at a rally at Homagama near Colombo on Saturday, after recent clashes between ruling People's Alliance (PA) and opposition United National Party (UNP) supporters.

Government is not taking steps to recover illegally used firearms and stem escalation of violence in the country, UNP leader Ranil Wickremesinghe said at a propaganda meeting in Hasalaka in central Sri Lanka on Saturday.

Police chief W.B. Rajaguru instructs officers in charge of police stations to take back fire arms issued to politicians during UNP rule, which ended in August 1994. This follows a number of incidents between PA and UNP supporters, where police believe weapons given to UNP politicians were used.
Navy repulses LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam) attack by squad of suicide bombers, on the eastern port of Trincomalee on Saturday.
Police in Hasalaka receive many complaints from UNP supporters regarding damage suffered during a rally on Saturday, at the hands of unidentified persons.
